solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mike quits Cambridge, running home for a lark?

indicators.note: the remaining letters run about into a new order

parts.note: the city, in full
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet; it quits, leaving CABRIDGE

explanation.surface: A man called Mike leaves Cambridge and heads home, perhaps just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a lark' pretends to mean 'for fun'; read literally, the lark is a songbird, and its home is a cage. The question mark flags that playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdcage is a home for a caged songbird such as a lark.

clue.text: Skirt father made lasts for countless parties

parts.note: something father made is made BY PA

indicators.note: take the last letters of the words that follow

parts.note: last letters of countlesS and partieS

explanation.surface: A father has sewn a skirt that lasts through countless parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' looks like a garment, but here it is the verb: to skirt a town is to go round it. 'Father made' is read as 'made by Pa'.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt something is to go around its edge, which is to bypass it.

clue.text: Perish climbing rocky peak

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word reads upwards, so it turns round

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A warning that anyone climbing a rocky peak might die up there.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a craggy hilltop in the south-west of England; written upwards in this down entry it gives ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: To rot is to decay, and food or wood left to perish rots.

clue.text: Notice sage right at the top?

parts.note: to clock something is to notice it (informal)
sage as an adjective = wise

explanation.surface: Spotting a wise figure sitting at the very top, perhaps of the hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the motion rather than the word: a hand turning clockwise moves to the right as it passes the top of the dial. The question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Clockwise movement heads rightwards when at the top of the circle.

clue.text: Irish mistake swallows for larger African species

indicators.note: the outer word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder; it goes round IR
IR is the standard abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: An Irishman's blunder with swallows, the birds, mistaken for a larger African kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallows' sits among bird-like words and reads as the migrating birds; it is the containment verb. 'Larger' is fair because a giraffe dwarfs the swallows of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is a tall African animal, a species far larger than any swallow.

clue.text: Forger's work that is collected by king

indicators.note: the king gathers the other letters inside himself

parts.note: CR = Carolus Rex, King Charles; it goes round the rest
op. = opus, a work
i.e. = id est, that is

explanation.surface: A forger's handiwork, which a king ends up collecting.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has': the forger has what follows. CR, from Carolus Rex on old coins and seals, is a less common abbreviation for king.
explanation.definitionFit: A forger copies documents or art, so is a copier.

clue.text: Duck pen in history

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O
a fold is a pen for sheep

explanation.surface: A duck kept in a pen, in some historical setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck and pen both look farmyard; the duck is a zero in cricket, shaped like the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Of old means in times past, in history.

clue.text: Thoughtless, stripping Artex inside during run-up to Christmas

indicators.note: take the outer letters off Artex

parts.note: in = during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: the stripped word goes within Advent

parts.note: Advent is the church season before Christmas

indicators.note: during a period is being in it

parts.note: Artex stripped of its outer A and X; RTE goes inside ADVE_NT

explanation.surface: Someone thoughtlessly scraping Artex off the walls just before Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: Artex is a textured plaster coating found on many British ceilings. IN + ADVE(RTE)NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inadvertent means unthinking or done without meaning to, so thoughtless.

clue.text: White lies disguised with grin

indicators.note: the letters are dressed up in a different order

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Harmless white lies covered with a grin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White lies' is a phrase that won't come apart easily, but 'White' alone is the definition: a white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white wine grape and the wine made from it.

clue.text: Result you note after baking

parts.note: U sounds like 'you', text-speak
a PS (postscript) is a note added after a letter
baking = very hot, as in a baking day

explanation.surface: Instructions to jot down the result once something comes out of the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is part of the note, not an order instruction: a postscript is literally a note after.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the upshot is how things finally turn out.

clue.text: Angelic boy too much out of bed on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows it back to front

parts.note: OTT = over the top, too much
up = out of bed

explanation.surface: A cherubic child who has been up and about far too much, seen in a mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: A putto is a winged cherub boy in Renaissance painting. OTT UP read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A putto is a chubby child angel in art, so an angelic boy.

clue.text: Roguish club made to look Victorian, perhaps opening for expats

parts.note: repro = reproduction, as in repro furniture made to look period
a bat is a club, in cricket or baseball

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of Expats

explanation.surface: A roguish club refitted in mock-Victorian style, maybe opening its doors to expats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society, and the surface builds a club-house; here it is a bat. Repro is short for reproduction, a copy made to look old.
explanation.definitionFit: Reprobate as an adjective means unprincipled, roguish.

clue.text: Max often removed hateful clothes, and there they are!

parts.note: shed = removed, as a snake sheds its skin; it goes round the next pieces
the peak is the maximum
oft is a poetic form of often
evil = hateful

explanation.surface: A man named Max often took off his hideous clothes, and there they lie!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like garments but is a verb: SHED clothes PEAK OFT, giving S(PEAK OFT)HED, then EVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: People say 'speak of the devil' when the person just mentioned appears: and there they are!

clue.text: Crooked seller denies disposing of one English antiquity in person

indicators.note: the letters are bent out of order
one letter is thrown away

parts.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
E = English; one of the four Es is disposed of

explanation.surface: A dishonest dealer denies getting rid of an English antique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Antiquity' and 'English' tempt towards antiques; the definition is about a person's age. SELLER DENIES has four Es and loses one.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderliness is the state of being old, the antiquity found in a person.

clue.text: Notice bad habit which professional might help you with

definitions.text: which professional might help you with

parts.note: an ad (advertisement) is a notice
a vice is a bad habit

explanation.surface: A bad habit you might see a professional to break.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests therapy for a habit; the definition is what the professional gives you.
explanation.definitionFit: Professionals such as lawyers help you with advice.

clue.text: You shouldn't have run home after mother, little monkey

indicators.note: run and home come after mother

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, what you say for 'you shouldn't have'
ma = mother
R = run, cricket scoring
in = at home

explanation.surface: A mother scolding her little monkey of a child for running home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have' reads as a scolding but is a polite thank-you: TA. 'Little monkey' is a naughty child in the surface and a real small monkey in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarin is a small South American monkey.

clue.text: Whiskers surely hurt except the end bits

indicators.note: 'except' leaves something out, and what it leaves out of ACHE is its end, the final E

parts.note: 'it must be' = surely it is
ACHE without its last letter
binary bits are 1 and 0, read as I and O

explanation.surface: Whiskers that must sting everywhere but at their tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End bits' looks like a phrase; 'the end' goes with 'except', and 'bits' alone means the binary digits 1 and 0.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustachio is a large moustache, a set of whiskers.

clue.text: Son diving in bubbled away gently underwater

parts.note: to simmer is to bubble gently; its leading S dives in, leaving IMMER_ED
S = son; it moves inside

explanation.surface: A son diving into water, sending bubbles gently to the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: The S is already at the front of SIMMERED; it moves from the start into the middle, turning SIMMERED into IMMERSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immersed is plunged under the water.

clue.text: Surface damage on minute gold musical ornament

indicators.note: in an across clue, the damage comes after the minute and gold

parts.note: M = minute
or is gold in heraldry
a dent is damage to a surface

explanation.surface: A scratch on a tiny golden trinket that plays music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' reads as tiny (my-NUTE) but is the unit of time, M. A mordent is a quick trill-like grace note.
explanation.definitionFit: A mordent is an ornament in music, a rapid alternation with the note next to it.

clue.text: Box that might arrive at any time?

definitions.text: Box that might arrive at any time?

parts.note: reads as a parcel or container; the setter means a police telephone box
reads as an unpredictable delivery; the setter means arriving in any era, by time travel

explanation.surface: A parcel that could turn up whenever it likes.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an unpredictable delivery. The TARDIS, from the British TV show Doctor Who, looks like a police telephone box and travels to any point in time.
explanation.definitionFit: The TARDIS is a box-shaped time machine that can arrive in any era.

clue.text: Easy catch but making it is relative

parts.note: in cricket a sitter is a very easy catch
the IT in S-IT-TER becomes IS

explanation.surface: An easy catch, though taking it matters to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A sitter is a simple chance in cricket that a fielder should not miss. Swap its IT for IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a sister is one kind of family relation, the surface's 'relative' having posed as the adjective.

clue.text: Learner spread chaos left and right

indicators.note: the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder
L = left
R = right

explanation.surface: A learner driver causing havoc on both sides of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learner' tempts you towards L for a learner driver; it is the definition, and L comes from 'left'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the older sense: a scholar was any pupil at school, someone learning.

clue.text: Due extended dry patch

definitions.note: 'Due' is used as a noun here: that which is owed
definitions.meaning: 'due' as a noun: what someone has earned, good or bad, their reward or punishment
a vast arid region such as the Sahara

explanation.surface: A payment that has run late, followed by a long dry spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the noun behind 'just deserts', pronounced like dessert: what you deserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert means what someone is due, and also a large arid region.

clue.text: Bad acne blights rude tattoo's location

indicators.note: the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

explanation.surface: A rude tattoo spoiled by a nasty outbreak of spots.
explanation.walkthrough: Tattoo suggests ink on skin; here it is the Edinburgh Military Tattoo, a show of military bands held each August on the castle esplanade.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by allusion: a tattoo here is a military display, and the most famous one is performed on the castle esplanade.

clue.text: Move, say, knight up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read upwards

parts.note: e.g. = for example, say
to dub someone is to knight them

explanation.surface: An order to move, perhaps promoting someone to a knighthood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight' is a verb here: the monarch dubs a knight with a sword. EG DUB, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually for a small shift, as in 'it won't budge'.

clue.text: Convenient telecoms facility spread far underground, south to west

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: laid = spread, as a table or a carpet
deep = far below the surface
S = south

explanation.surface: A phone network whose cables are laid deep underground running south-west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South to west' looks like a compass direction for the cables; 'south' gives S and 'to west' tells you to reverse LAID DEEP S.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed dial is a phone feature that calls a stored number with one press, a convenience.

clue.text: As a result of this coming through kitchen ceiling

indicators.note: the answer shows through the words that follow

parts.note: kitcHEN CEiling

explanation.surface: A leak coming through the kitchen ceiling, with the damage that follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures water coming through a ceiling; the phrase is the hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: hence introduces a consequence, like 'therefore'.

clue.text: Score for your team immediately after kick-off

definitions.text: Score for your team immediately after kick-off

parts.note: reads as a goal your side has just scored; the setter means the scoreline itself
a moment into a football match, before anyone has had time to score

explanation.surface: A fan asking how their side is doing a moment into the game.
explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a question about a goal just scored; in fact nobody has scored anything yet, so the score is nil.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil means nothing, the score of any team at the start of a match.

clue.text: Frustrated guy with kids stuck with that woman

indicators.note: a dad stuck with someone has them lodged in his company

parts.note: a man with children is a dad; he goes round SHE
she = that woman

explanation.surface: A fed-up father, lumbered with the children and with her.
explanation.walkthrough: DA(SHE)D: the dad holds her in the middle. Dashed hopes are frustrated ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashed, as in dashed hopes, means frustrated or thwarted.

clue.text: Bear allowed little running water

parts.note: to brook is to tolerate or bear, usually in 'brook no argument'
let = allowed

explanation.surface: A bear permitted to paddle in a small stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal; it is the verb meaning tolerate, BROOK.
explanation.definitionFit: A brooklet is a small brook, a little stream of running water.
